currentContext.business: IKIO is a B2B Original Design Manufacturer that designs, engineers and manufactures customised LED lighting and electronics solutions end-to-end, from concept and design through prototyping to large-scale manufacturing and delivery, primarily for customers in the FMEG (Fast Moving Electrical Goods) sector. Historically a lighting ODM, the company has broadened into automotive electronics, product display and refrigeration systems, hearables/wearables consumer electronics, energy products (solar panels, lithium batteries), and wider electronic manufacturing services (OEM/ODM), managing a portfolio of over 3,000 SKUs.

Automotive LED lighting: Automotive lighting for two-wheelers and four-wheelers (exterior and interior, OEM/ODM)
Product display and refrigeration system: Product display lighting for commercial refrigeration
Refrigeration display systems for organised retail
Lighting for the Indian EMS market
Energy solutions/RV/others: Rotary switches and fan regulators & assembly

currentContext.strengths: Decades of experience and deep backward integration in LED lighting, providing the base for expansion into automotive electronics|End-to-end ODM capability spanning design, engineering, prototyping and large-scale manufacturing, supporting a portfolio of 3,000+ SKUs across multiple categories|Diversified, export-oriented footprint via dedicated overseas platforms - Royalux LLC (USA) for North America and Ritech Holdings/Royalux FZCO (UAE) as the Middle East gateway|Net debt-free balance sheet cited as providing financial flexibility to fund the Block II commercialisation and further expansion|Diversifying revenue mix reducing reliance on the ODM home lighting segment, with the 'Other Business' segment (hearables/wearables, product display, energy, automotive) now the dominant growth engine
currentContext.strategies: Expand product portfolio by strengthening high-growth electronics and energy-related categories through internal capability development|Diversify geographic base by reducing customer concentration risk, expanding the customer base and entering new international geographies|Pursue design-led innovation by investing in in-house R&D (50+ professional team) to co-develop customised products, shorten development timelines and expand into adjacent categories without separate design ecosystems|Enhance production footprint by scaling capacity and platform scalability through the multi-phase Noida Greenfield Project|Strengthen ESG and operational excellence by integrating sustainable practices and operational discipline for long-term resilience|Actively pursue ASEAN expansion by securing regulatory approvals for entry into the Philippines, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia and Singapore|Consolidate the Hearables and Wearables (HWA) business vertical directly under the parent company (effective April 2026), discontinuing it at subsidiary Royalux Lighting Private Limited
currentContext.expansion: IKIO's principal expansion project is the Noida Greenfield Facility (approximately 5 lakh sq. ft. total), executed in three phases: Block I (~2 lakh sq. ft.), which commenced commercial production in May 2024 and supports LED home lighting, solar panels and new product lines; Block II (~2 lakh sq. ft.), nearing completion and expected to be commercialised by Q1 FY27, with roughly 60% of its space earmarked for hearables/wearables and 40% for automotive lighting and electronics; and Block III (~1 lakh sq. ft.), currently under construction with a focus on specialised, high-value product categories and no disclosed completion date. Once all blocks are operational, the company states total manufacturing capacity (across its five facilities, including the SIDCUL, Haridwar unit of 42,517 sq. ft.) will reach approximately 8 lakh sq. ft., strengthening export capability and enabling new domestic products such as LED home lighting and solar panel systems. The facility also carries a 200 KVA rooftop solar installation for captive power. Beyond organic capacity, the company expanded its footprint inorganically during the year through the 88% acquisition of Gravus Tech Private Limited (December 2025) to strengthen marketing/distribution reach, and through incorporation of Royalux General Trading LLC (UAE) to widen its Middle East trading operations.

risks.note: The CFO role changed twice within the reporting window - Mr. Subhash Chand Agrawal (till June 30, 2024), then Mr. Atul Kumar Jain (till July 1, 2025), before Mr. Sanjeet Singh was appointed CFO in August 2025; the Deputy CFO, Mr. Naveen Bhatia, has also tendered resignation effective June 30, 2026, indicating repeated churn in the finance leadership function.

risks.risk: Concentration of executive roles in one individual
risks.note: Mr. Sanjeet Singh simultaneously holds the positions of Whole-Time Director, Chief Financial Officer and Group Chief Executive Officer, concentrating operational, financial and executive authority in a single officer rather than separating these functions.

The Board created and filled a new Chief Information Security Officer position (Mr. Narendra Prasad, appointed May 2, 2026) on the recommendation of the Risk Management Committee, and the Committee's charter explicitly names information and cyber security risk as a category it must identify and mitigate.

Mrs. Rachana Chowdhary, the Company's sole Non-Executive Woman Independent Director, resigned effective April 4, 2026; her replacement (Ms. Madhu Pandit) was appointed only as an Additional Director pending shareholder approval, leaving a temporary gap in the mandated women-independent-director composition.

risks.risk: Broad, enumerated enterprise risk categories monitored by the Board
risks.note: The Risk Management Committee's terms of reference formally cover financial, operational, sectoral, sustainability/ESG-related, information and cyber security risk, and any other risk the Committee determines material - signalling multi-dimensional risk exposure typical of a fast-diversifying, multi-subsidiary electronics manufacturer, though the specific risk register itself is not detailed in this section.

one-line thesis: IKIO has successfully diversified from a lighting-only ODM to a multi-segment integrated technology player, with non-lighting revenue now at 77% of Q4 FY26 sales and global exports rising 53% YoY; the scaling of new verticals (Hearables, Automotive, Energy) and greenfield capacity is driving margin expansion despite front-loaded costs, positioning the company for sustained 20-22% revenue growth and 15-16% EBITDA margins in FY27.

hero.oneLiner: IKIO Technologies Limited (formerly IKIO Lighting Limited) is an innovation-driven Original Design Manufacturer (ODM) rooted in LED lighting that has diversified into energy solutions, product display systems and consumer electronics for global B2B customers.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: IKIO Technologies Limited (formerly IKIO Lighting Limited) is an innovation-driven Original Design Manufacturer (ODM) rooted in LED lighting that has diversified into energy solutions, product display systems and consumer electronics for global B2B customers.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: IKIO is a B2B Original Design Manufacturer that designs, engineers and manufactures customised LED lighting and electronics solutions end-to-end, from concept and design through prototyping to large-scale manufacturing and delivery, primarily for customers in the FMEG (Fast Moving Electrical Goods) sector. Historically a lighting ODM, the company has broadened into automotive electronics, product display and refrigeration systems, hearables/wearables consumer electronics, energy products (solar panels, lithium batteries), and wider electronic manufacturing services (OEM/ODM), managing a portfolio of over 3,000 SKUs.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- IKIO Solutions Private Limited (ISPL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%); primary domestic manufacturing arm managing design, fabrication and assembly of mechanical components for lighting, solar and EMS categories
- Royalux Lighting Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (100%); focuses on product display lighting, IPS controllers and specialised electrical components for commercial refrigeration
- Royalux Exports Private Limited (REPL) — subsidiary: Wholly owned step-down subsidiary (100%); focused on high-growth exports including LED lights, solar panels, lithium batteries and RV product lines
- Royalux LLC, USA — subsidiary: Wholly owned step-down subsidiary of IKIO Solutions Private Limited (100%); dedicated platform for the North American market providing local client servicing, product customisation and logistical support
- Ritech Holding Limited, UAE — subsidiary: Wholly owned step-down subsidiary (100%); serves as the expansion gateway for the Middle East
- Royalux FZCO, UAE — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary of Ritech Holding Limited (51%); engages in trading of high-end chandeliers, lighting fixtures and electrical components (Dubai); has a joint venture with AG Investments to improve regional market access
- Gravus Tech Private Limited — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary via IKIO Solutions Private Limited (88%), acquired December 8, 2025; to be used for marketing and distribution of IKIO Group products
- Royalux General Trading LLC, UAE — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary of Ritech Holding Limited (51%); newly incorporated for general trading activities to expand the Group's international trading operations
- Raina Metal Tech Private Limited — related party: Enterprise in which key managerial personnel and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence
- Inko Technologies — related party: Enterprise in which key managerial personnel and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence
- IKIO LED Lighting LLC — related party: Enterprise in which key managerial personnel and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence
- Singh Enterprises — related party: Enterprise in which key managerial personnel and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence
- Krishna Computech International Private Limited — related party: Enterprise in which key managerial personnel and their relatives are able to exercise significant influence

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Lighting: 23% of Q4 revenue (down from prior years), ODM Home Lighting still with Signify but diversifying to other top 5 Indian brands; Commercial/Refrigeration: leading supplier; Automotive: new aftermarket LED source supplier to multinational brands (NDAs in place); Hearables/Wearables: 60% OEM, transitioning to ODM, margins in high single digits targeting double digits; Energy: solar inverters + batteries launched; EMS: new vertical in Tower 1, supplying Honeywell for PA systems and sensors

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **LED lighting solutions:** High-end home decorative LED lights, Facade lighting, Indoor and outdoor lightings, In-store lightings, High-end architectural lightings
- **Consumer electronics:** Neckbands, TWS earbuds, Bluetooth speakers, Smartwatches, Headsets
- **Automotive LED lighting:** Automotive lighting for two-wheelers and four-wheelers (exterior and interior, OEM/ODM)
- **Product display and refrigeration systems:** Product display lighting for commercial refrigeration, Refrigeration display systems for organised retail, Lighting for the Indian EMS market
- **Energy solutions/RV/others:** Solar panels, Lithium batteries, USB chargers, RV-specific LED lights, ABS pipes for RV infrastructure, Rotary switches and fan regulators & assembly
- **Electronic manufacturing services (OEM/ODM):** Automotive, E-mobility, Home appliances, Consumer electronics, Home automation, Telecom, Industrial automation, Power electronics

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: No formal order book; revenue driven by ODM planning with customer volume forecasts and pipeline, not contractual backlog

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: 20-22% YoY in FY27; margin: 15-16% EBITDA; order inflow: expected to grow with new customers in Automotive, Honeywell EMS, and Middle East lighting; capex/commissioning: Block II of 2 lakh sq.ft greenfield facility to be commissioned by end of Q1 FY27, total capex funded via IPO proceeds

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into U.S. solar and electronics market (ready plan, delayed by geopolitics); entry into premium European residential lighting; scaling Honeywell EMS contracts; leveraging 5 factories for fungible production across verticals; potential for further M&A in distribution or component tech

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) sector continues to see strong growth momentum, supported by the 'China+1' strategy, increasing localisation, expanding domestic consumption and government PLI schemes
- India's EMS market, valued at USD 33 billion in 2024, is expected to grow at a CAGR of approximately 30% to reach USD 155 billion by 2030, aided by a sector shift from Low-Mix High-Volume assembly to High-Mix Low-Volume manufacturing with greater value addition
- Rising demand across consumer electronics, automotive electronics, industrial automation, smart devices and energy-efficient solutions is strengthening India's position as a preferred global manufacturing destination
- Emerging opportunities from automotive lighting, wearables, hearables, industrial electronics and exports are expected to support long-term industry expansion
- Government initiatives such as PLI schemes and the broader push toward domestic manufacturing provide a supportive environment for expanding capacity, deepening localisation and building globally competitive capabilities, particularly through participation in the PLI scheme for white goods
- The 'Other Business' segment (hearables/wearables, product display lighting, energy solutions, automotive) is the Company's dominant growth engine, growing its share of consolidated revenue to approximately 71% (from 57% in FY25)
- Revenue from Outside India is a key growth driver, rising 53% YoY on strong Middle East (Dubai) traction, even as US demand faced tariff-policy related uncertainty
- Profitability is expected to benefit from operating leverage as scale expands and business mix evolves toward higher-margin non-lighting categories
- The Hearables and Wearables segment recorded strong growth momentum during the year, supported by increased client orders, reflecting growing confidence of leading brands in the Company's ODM capabilities
- Multiple leading Indian brands are now supported by dedicated infrastructure at the Noida facility, enabling closer integration and scalable execution
- New domestic and international customers were onboarded during the year, with consumer electronics emerging as a key growth driver

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin expansion from 13% (FY26) to 15-16% (FY27 guidance) driven by operating leverage as new verticals scale; current margins depressed by front-loaded R&D, capex, and 2,500+ headcount; raw material cost inflation (aluminum, copper) partially offset by design flexibility and customer price adjustments

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: IPO proceeds fully allocated to capex for manufacturing expansion; acquisition of 88% stake in Gravus Tech for GTM expansion; no dividends or buybacks mentioned; focus on reinvestment into R&D and new verticals

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: IKIO's principal expansion project is the Noida Greenfield Facility (approximately 5 lakh sq. ft. total), executed in three phases: Block I (~2 lakh sq. ft.), which commenced commercial production in May 2024 and supports LED home lighting, solar panels and new product lines; Block II (~2 lakh sq. ft.), nearing completion and expected to be commercialised by Q1 FY27, with roughly 60% of its space earmarked for hearables/wearables and 40% for automotive lighting and electronics; and Block III (~1 lakh sq. ft.), currently under construction with a focus on specialised, high-value product categories and no disclosed completion date. Once all blocks are operational, the company states total manufacturing capacity (across its five facilities, including the SIDCUL, Haridwar unit of 42,517 sq. ft.) will reach approximately 8 lakh sq. ft., strengthening export capability and enabling new domestic products such as LED home lighting and solar panel systems. The facility also carries a 200 KVA rooftop solar installation for captive power. Beyond organic capacity, the company expanded its footprint inorganically during the year through the 88% acquisition of Gravus Tech Private Limited (December 2025) to strengthen marketing/distribution reach, and through incorporation of Royalux General Trading LLC (UAE) to widen its Middle East trading operations.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident, strategic, and forward-looking; management emphasizes ODM solutioning over product selling, highlights operational flexibility, and frames challenges (geopolitics, margins) as temporary; tone is bullish on long-term diversification and global positioning

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Decades of experience and deep backward integration in LED lighting, providing the base for expansion into automotive electronics
- End-to-end ODM capability spanning design, engineering, prototyping and large-scale manufacturing, supporting a portfolio of 3,000+ SKUs across multiple categories
- Diversified, export-oriented footprint via dedicated overseas platforms - Royalux LLC (USA) for North America and Ritech Holdings/Royalux FZCO (UAE) as the Middle East gateway
- Net debt-free balance sheet cited as providing financial flexibility to fund the Block II commercialisation and further expansion
- Diversifying revenue mix reducing reliance on the ODM home lighting segment, with the 'Other Business' segment (hearables/wearables, product display, energy, automotive) now the dominant growth engine

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: U.S. market delays due to geopolitical tensions and tariffs; supply chain disruptions from Middle East instability; margin pressure from raw material inflation; execution risk in scaling new verticals (Hearables, EMS, Energy); customer concentration risk in legacy Home Lighting (Signify) despite diversification

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Hearables/Wearables segment is being moved from subsidiary to parent company to streamline ops — signals strategic prioritization; company is not competing with Lumax/FIEM but supplying LED sources to their products — Tier 2 supplier with high-value design IP; 80-85% of business is ODM, not OEM, indicating strong design IP and customer lock-in; solar + battery offering is bundled with EMS, creating end-to-end energy solutions

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Expand product portfolio by strengthening high-growth electronics and energy-related categories through internal capability development
- Diversify geographic base by reducing customer concentration risk, expanding the customer base and entering new international geographies
- Pursue design-led innovation by investing in in-house R&D (50+ professional team) to co-develop customised products, shorten development timelines and expand into adjacent categories without separate design ecosystems
- Enhance production footprint by scaling capacity and platform scalability through the multi-phase Noida …

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Name change] Now IKIO Technologies Limited, "Formerly known as IKIO Lighting Limited" (CIN L31401DL2016PLC292884), reflecting the shift beyond lighting.
- [Customer anchors] Deck names Philips India (Signify) as the customer for whom a dedicated LED supply facility was set up, and Honeywell India as the customer for wiring devices.
- [Board] Chairman & MD Hardeep Singh; Sanjeet Singh holds the combined Whole Time Director, CEO and CFO roles; four independent directors including a former CMD of Steel Authority of India and a former MD & CEO of Vijaya Bank.
- [Policy tailwinds cited] China+1 supply-chain diversification and PLI-led localisation are named as the structural drivers enabling entry into higher-value EMS, alongside a stated sector shift from Low-Mix High-Volume to High-Mix Low-Volume manufacturing.
